clue.text: Decline something worthless

definitions.meaning: to decline an offer is to turn it down, the verb sense
rubbish or waste, the noun sense, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.surface: Someone turns down an offer of a piece of junk.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to say no to an offer; the noun is household rubbish, things of no value thrown away.

clue.text: Lying about improvement in health?

parts.note: reads as someone telling lies about getting better, but means a treatment of lying in bed doing nothing to recover

explanation.surface: Someone fibbing about how well they are recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like telling untruths; here it means lying down, and 'about' means idling around, a Victorian remedy of enforced bed rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian medical regimen of bed rest and idleness prescribed for recovery, especially from nervous illness.

clue.text: Some fare badly? That's terrible

indicators.note: fare that is done badly is mangled, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A diner complains that some of the food is poor, which is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SOMEFARE; 'That's' is a link leading to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fearsome inspires dread, so it can be called frightful or terrible.

clue.text: Ringlets, looking artificial but absolutely genuine

indicators.note: curls that look artificial are not in their natural form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's curls look fake but are actually real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking artificial' rearranges RINGLETS; the surface sets up artificial against genuine as a contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling describes something of solid, thoroughly reliable quality, like sterling silver of full standard purity.

clue.text: The Case of the Unused Sword

definitions.text: The Case of the Unused Sword

parts.words: The Case of the Unused Sword
parts.note: reads like the title of a detective story, but literally names the sheath a blade rests in when not in use

explanation.surface: A Sherlock Holmes-style mystery title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a detective investigation; it is a literal holder for a blade that is not being drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath of leather or metal that holds a blade, hanging from a belt when the weapon is not drawn.

clue.text: Can look inside brownish-coloured melon

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for look goes inside the colour word, splitting it

parts.note: taupe is a brownish-grey colour
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone peers into a melon with brown skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts LO within TAUPE to give TALOUPE, after CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded variety of muskmelon with orange flesh and ribbed rind.

clue.text: Finish we hear beside this sea

definitions.text: Finish we hear beside this sea

parts.words: Finish we hear beside this sea
parts.note: Finish sounds like Finnish, and Finland lies on the coast of the sea meant

explanation.surface: An ending heard beside the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish' looks like an ending; said aloud it is Finnish, and Finland borders this northern European sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern European sea bordered by Finland, Sweden, Poland and the Baltic states.

clue.text: A loose woman relative?

parts.note: to loose something is to set it free, which is to untie it

explanation.surface: A promiscuous female family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like an adjective describing the woman; it is a verb meaning to unfasten.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister, or an uncle's wife, often called this affectionately.

clue.text: Day in the city-an African one

parts.note: urban means of or belonging to the city

explanation.surface: A day spent in town, in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside URBAN. DURBAN is a port city in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A major port in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, so a city on that continent.

clue.text: Investor receiving money from ship in nefarious trade

indicators.note: the investor takes in the money, so its letter goes inside

parts.note: a saver puts money aside, an investor
L stands for pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: An investor makes money from a ship used in a wicked business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts L (pound) inside SAVER. The nefarious trade is the slave trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel used to carry captives in the slave trade bears this name.

clue.text: A single ship is a joke, in brief

parts.note: a single thing is one
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: One vessel is said to be a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in brief' is part of the definition: a quip delivered in a single sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A short quip or witticism delivered in a single sentence.

clue.text: Move king to safety in stronghold

definitions.meaning: in chess, the king and rook swap positions to tuck the king away
a fortified building such as a fortress

explanation.surface: A ruler retreats to a fortress for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a real king fleeing; the first definition is the chess move.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess this is the move tucking the monarch behind a rook; the noun is a fortified medieval building.

clue.text: Fawlty in charge of a magnificent church

parts.note: Basil Fawlty is the hotelier in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers

explanation.surface: A sitcom hotelier running a grand church.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil Fawlty is the hotel owner in the 1970s British sitcom Fawlty Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, grand church, especially one granted special ceremonial privileges by the Pope.

clue.text: Put up with whisky maker's inactivity

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
a still is the apparatus used to distil whisky

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a distiller's laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete halt, where nothing moves or progresses.

clue.text: Thoughtfulness of maiden in state of downfall

indicators.note: the maiden's letter is placed within the word for ruin

parts.note: ruination is a state of being ruined
M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden over

explanation.surface: A ruined young woman becomes reflective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside RUINATION; M for maiden is a cricket scoring abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep, pondering thought, like a cow chewing the cud over an idea.

clue.text: Attend demonstration to provide evidence

parts.note: to go to an event is to attend it
a show is a demonstration or display

explanation.surface: Turning up at a demonstration proves a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'it goes to show' means it proves or serves as evidence.

clue.text: Better water found in America

definitions.meaning: Lake ..., the largest of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Better water is found in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means higher in quality; the second is the greatest of the Great Lakes on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Time long ago when one was in the theatre

indicators.note: one is placed within the word for the theatre profession

parts.note: the stage is the acting profession
taken as written

explanation.surface: A time long past when someone was an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ONE inside STAGE; 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period when humans made tools from flint and rock.

clue.text: Final result-cup trodden and smashed

indicators.note: a cup trodden on is broken to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cup is stamped on and broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' rearranges CUPTRODDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The finished outcome of a process, what you get at the conclusion.

clue.text: Mountain guide uses unusual phrase

indicators.note: an unusual phrase is one put out of its normal form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A climbing guide uses odd expressions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges PHRASE; 'uses' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Himalayan people famed as porters and guides on Everest expeditions.

clue.text: Avoided the fog, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard, so the word for fog is said aloud

parts.note: mist is a light fog

explanation.surface: Someone escaped the fog, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' makes MIST sound like MISSED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have missed something is to have dodged or escaped it.

clue.text: Badly managed, but I shall be in the race

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I shall
to run is to take part in a race

explanation.surface: Someone complains the event is poorly run but enters anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: I'LL plus RUN gives ILL-RUN; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Poorly organised or administered, as of a business.

clue.text: Hot and stuffy, without any cover

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a stuffy room is airless

explanation.surface: Hot, stuffy and uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link joining H to AIRLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bald or smooth-skinned, having no growth on the head or body.

clue.text: Up-to date method to lead the Navy

indicators.note: the method word goes first, leading the navy abbreviation

parts.note: a mode is a way or method
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A fresh approach to leading the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lead' puts MODE in front of RN, the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to present times, contemporary.

clue.text: Hold back holiday-wet weather

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A rainy holiday keeps people indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb or keep something in check.

clue.text: Quiet fib returned by a girl

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: the word for fib is sent back, reading backwards

parts.note: a lie is a fib

explanation.surface: A girl answers back with a hushed untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LIE into ELI; 'by' is a link. SHEILA is Australian slang for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a young woman.

clue.text: With passion, read out scripture extremely loudly

indicators.note: read out of order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: NT is the New Testament

indicators.note: the extreme letters of loudly are its first and last

explanation.surface: Someone reads the Bible aloud very loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges READ into ARDE; 'extremely' takes L and Y, the first and last letters of 'loudly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervently, with burning enthusiasm.

clue.text: Put ball into play, capturing point with deflection

indicators.note: the serve takes in the point, so its letter goes inside

parts.note: to serve in tennis is to put the ball into play
W is west, a compass point

explanation.surface: A tennis serve wins a point with a swerving ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts W (west, a compass point) inside SERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden veering off course, a turning aside.
